full_judgment: 16. With reference to the above terms of the waqf deed Mr. Sobhan submitted that the right claimed by the respondents satisfied the provisions of sub-rule (2) of rule 1 of Order XL. On this point he referred to two decisions, namely, A.I.R. 1936 Allahabad (FB) 495 (Anandi Lal Vs. Ram Sarup) and A.I.R. 1945 Cal. 298 (Sree Radha Ballav Jew Vs. Bibhuti). In A.I.R. 1936 Allahabad 495 it has been observed that general power under sub-rule (1) of rule 1 of Order XL has been curtailed by sub-rule (2) of rule 1. Powers conferred by sub-rule (1) cannot be exercised when they come in conflict with the provisions of Sub-rule (2). There is, therefore, no authority in the court to remove from the possession or custody of property 'any person' whom any party to the suit has not a present right so to remove. The words 'any person' are general and have been used in a wide sense and are fully comprehensive to include persons who are parties and persons who are not parties. In A.I.R. 1945 Cal. 298 it has been held that Order XL, Rule 1(1)(b) gives the court the power to remove any person from possession. Order XL, Rule 1(2) covers only the case of removal of a person from possession who is not a party to the suit. Order XL, rule 1(2) is a limitation on the power of the Court as defined in sub-rule (1)(b) of Rule 1 of Order XL. It is an exception, so its effect must be taken to be the normal effect of a provision which is in the nature of proviso. It limits the operation of the main provision. Order XL, rule 1(2) therefore means that a person in possession cannot be removed whom none of the parties to the suit has the present right to remove and is no bar to the removal of any party to the suit. There is apparent conflict in these two decisions and in fact the decision in A.I.R. 1936 Allahabad (FB) 495 has been dissented from.
